I will plant winter wheat and summer maize on the same land. Where I farm in Quzhou County, that is the most familiar and steady way for me to make use of the full year. I know this rotation fits our climate, fits our irrigation conditions, and gives me grain for a reliable sale instead of taking bigger risk on a crop I do not know as well. I will keep the whole area in grain because I want stable yield, easier field work, and simpler decisions. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen for strong tillering, add phosphorus and potassium to support roots and grain filling, irrigate at the key stages, and keep weeds and disease under control with a small number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep maize on the same area, reduce tillage to save time and moisture, feed it mainly with nitrogen plus some phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate when the crop is under stress. I am choosing this plan because it is the most practical, lowest-risk, and most profitable path I would trust myself to manage through the whole year.
